name: sr1a_supersedes_stale_modiv
why: The ticket-020 case, taken from a real Ramsey parcel. MOD-IV's DEED_DATE for 41 Ramsey Ave reads '200916' (2020-09-16) — the *prior* owner's deed — while the NJ SR1A sales register records the parcel selling on 2026-06-01. Before this source existed the door scored 15 and the 100-point Mover group was structurally unearnable town-wide (the newest deed anywhere in the MOD-IV extract was 2024-12-06). Pins two things at once: that the fresher register wins the deed, and that winning it is worth exactly the 61-90 day band and not the top one — the state's recording-and-publication lag means a run can never see a sale newer than a few weeks.

resolution.why: The `parcel` above is the *merged* record the score engine is handed, not what either source carries alone. This block is what it was merged from, and tests/test_resolve.py replays it through the real resolver.
resolution.rule: the sales register supersedes the parcel record only when its deed is strictly newer, and the whole record moves together — date, price and usability code

expect.arithmetic: mover 70 (2026-06-01 is 74 days before as_of -> the 61-90 day band) + hires_out 0 (no permits) + capacity 15 (840,700 >= 743,350 median, and below 1.5x = 1,115,025) + need 0 (built 2007 = 19 yrs < 30; 0.34 acre < 0.5; no vision) + modifier 0 = 85

evidence_must_include.reason: the register supplied a deed inside the mover window, so the group fires where MOD-IV alone left it at zero

evidence_must_exclude.reason: a door that just sold is not a long-tenure door; scoring MOD-IV's 2020 date would have produced this line instead

comparative.baseline: the same parcel scored from MOD-IV's own DEED_DATE=200916, as every run before ticket 020 did
comparative.why: 70 of this door's 85 points exist only because a fresher deed source was added. That gap is the ticket's whole justification, and it is the difference between a door a rep visits and one they never see.
